Asset Navigator Dashboard — User Guide

This guide explains the Asset Navigator Dashboard, which provides a comprehensive interface for browsing and exploring infrastructure topology stored in GraphDB. The dashboard combines a two-column navigation panel with three specialized views to help you understand your asset relationships and details.

TabWidget TypePurpose
TopologytopologyInteractive graph visualization with nodes and edges
Node Detailsportal_summaryDetailed attribute summary for the selected asset
RelationsgraphdbInbound and outbound connection table for the selected node

1. What This Dashboard Does

The Asset Navigator Dashboard helps you explore your infrastructure topology by providing:

  • Two-column navigation — Browse assets by type (e.g. Application, Webserver) and select individual nodes
  • Topology view — Visualize assets and their connections in an interactive graph with pan and zoom
  • Node details — View comprehensive attributes and metadata for any selected asset
  • Relationships view — See all inbound and outbound connections in a structured table

All three tabs work together — when you select a node from the navigation panel, all views update automatically to show information about that asset.

2. Dashboard Overview

The Asset Navigator Dashboard displays an interactive topology visualization with three main tabs. The topology graph shows nodes representing assets (shown as circular icons with labels), and edges showing connections between them. The graph supports pan, zoom, and node selection. A Nodes panel on the right side lists all visible nodes with their layer, type, and other attributes.

3. Topology Tab

The Topology tab displays an interactive graph visualization of your infrastructure. Nodes represent assets (shown as circular icons with labels), and edges show connections between them. The graph supports pan, zoom, and node selection. A Nodes panel on the right side lists all visible nodes with their layer, type, and other attributes. Clicking any node in the graph or table opens detailed information in the side panel.

Use Topology when you want to visualize asset connectivity, explore network topology, or understand how assets relate to each other graphically.

Don't use Topology when you need detailed attribute lists (use Node Details) or a precise typed relationship table (use Relations).

Widget Configuration (JSON Dashboard Def.)

The Topology widget is configured with widget_type: "topology". Key configuration includes:

  • nodes_report — Defines the side panel table showing all nodes
  • edges_report — Defines the table showing all connections
  • stack_definition — Specifies the GraphDB database, nodes stream, edges collection, and graph name
  • nodeSelectionPreview — Opens node details dashboard when clicking nodes
  • edgeSelectionPreview — Opens edge details dashboard when clicking edges

4. Node Details Tab

The Node Details tab shows a comprehensive summary of all attributes and metadata for the currently selected node. This includes all fields stored in GraphDB for that asset, such as node ID, node label, application name, database keys, and any custom properties. The data is displayed in a clean, readable format with field names and values.

Use Node Details when you need to see all properties of an asset, verify configuration details, review identifiers, or audit node metadata.

Don't use Node Details when you need to see connections (use Relations) or visualize topology (use Topology).

Widget Configuration (JSON Dashboard Def.)

The Node Details widget is configured with widget_type: "portal_summary". This widget automatically displays all available fields from the selected node's data in GraphDB. The node is identified using the NODE_ID template variable, which is populated from the navigation panel selection.

5. Relations Tab

The Relations tab presents a structured table view of all inbound and outbound connections for the selected node. The view is organized into collapsible sections (e.g. "Connected to 1 Webserver(s)") showing connection direction and neighbor type. Each row displays the Node Type, Node ID, and Node Label of connected assets, making it easy to understand dependencies.

Use Relations when you need a complete list of connections, want to audit dependencies, or need to see typed relationship details in a table format.

Don't use Relations when you need visual context (use Topology) or detailed node attributes (use Node Details).

Widget Configuration (JSON Dashboard Def.)

The Relations widget is configured with widget_type: "graphdb". Key settings include:

  • db_name — The GraphDB database to query (e.g. topology_training)
  • nodes_collection — Collection containing node data
  • edges_collection — Collection containing edge/relationship data
  • graph_name — Named graph defining the topology structure
  • relation_map — Configuration defining valid relationship types and directions

6. Navigation Panel

The left navigation panel provides a two-column browser for selecting assets:

  • First column (tree_data) — Groups nodes by type (e.g. Application, Webserver). Configured with column_name: "node_type" in the JSON Dashboard Def.
  • Second column (tree_detail) — Lists individual nodes within the selected type, showing Node ID and Node Name. Configured with display_column: "node_label" in the JSON Dashboard Def.

Features include:

  • Search box — Quickly find nodes by name (enabled with showSearchBox: true)
  • Node icons — Visual type indicators for each asset (enabled with showNodeIcon: true)
  • Auto-selection — The first node is automatically selected when you open the dashboard

7. End-to-End Workflow

  1. Open the Asset Navigator Dashboard.
  2. In the left navigation panel, select a node type from the first column (e.g. Application, Webserver).
  3. Select a specific node from the second column by Node Name — all three tabs refresh automatically.
  4. Use the Topology tab to visualize the asset's connections in an interactive graph. Click and drag to pan, scroll to zoom.
  5. Use the Node Details tab to review all attributes, identifiers, and properties of the selected asset.
  6. Use the Relations tab to see a complete table of inbound and outbound connections, grouped by connection type.
  7. Click on any node in the Topology Nodes panel or Relations table to navigate to that asset and update all views.

8. Tips & Tricks

Pro Tips:
  • Use the search box in the navigation panel to quickly jump to a specific asset by name.
  • In the Topology view, use the Nodes side panel to filter and search for specific assets in the graph.
  • The Edges panel in the Topology tab shows all connections — useful for understanding relationship types.
  • Click the expand/collapse icons in the Relations tab to show or hide connection groups.
  • Adjust the time filter at the top if certain nodes don't appear — they may be outside the selected time window.
Common Pitfalls:
  • Navigation panel empty: Check the time filter — node timestamps may be outside the selected window.
  • Tabs show no data after selection: Verify the node ID is being passed correctly via the NODE_ID template variable.
  • Topology view blank: Check that the edges collection and graph name are configured correctly in the stack definition.
  • Relations tab empty: Verify the relation map is configured for the selected node type in the GraphDB configuration.
  • Search not working: Ensure showSearchBox: true is set in the navigation_dashboards configuration.

11. JSON Dashboard Def. Overview

The Asset Navigator is configured as a navigation-dashboard type, which combines a two-column navigator with tabbed content. Key sections in the JSON Dashboard Def.:

  • navigation_dashboards — Defines the two-column navigation panel structure:
    • tree_data — First column configuration (groups by node_type)
    • tree_detail — Second column configuration (displays node_label)
    • showNodeIcon and showSearchBox — Enable icons and search
  • template_variables — Maps the selected node ID from the navigation context to NODE_ID variable used by widgets
  • dashboard_sections[] — Contains the three tabs:
    • Topology tab with widget_type: "topology"
    • Node Details tab with widget_type: "portal_summary"
    • Relations tab with widget_type: "graphdb"
  • dashboard_generator — Optional attachment to display the JSON Dashboard Def. codeblock next to each widget in live edit mode
